placements.title: A calibration claim is only as strong as the reference it was checked against
placements.frame: What reference standard was the instrument checked against, and does the calibration hold across the full band it will be used in?
placements.why: The envelope's contribution is not the 88.4 MHz figure itself — that is position-grain evidence — but the standing subject it evidences: that an observatory instrument's calibration is stated together with the reference plates it was verified against and the band over which it holds. That is a subject future envelopes (other instruments, other reference sets, recalibrations) will keep feeding, so it passes the grain test as a leaf rather than a fact. Nothing exists in the supplied structure to reuse, and nothing is close enough to extend, so it stands foundational.

mints.name: InstrumentCalibration
mints.title: Instrument calibration, the frequency it is set at, and the reference plates it is verified against
mints.why: The envelope's leaf and its position are both about one subject — an instrument's calibration state and the verification that backs it — and no existing stratum holds that grouping. Naming it in the organization's own words (instrument, calibration, reference plates) gives later instruments and recalibrations a place to connect.

connections.why: The leaf's whole subject is calibration stated with its verification reference and band, which is exactly what this stratum groups.
The position holds the concrete calibration state — 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates, holding across the observing band — the instance this stratum collects.
